svg.title: Mockup D — Production Stage world-state language at management distance (Visual Direction 01)
svg.desc: Non-production reference mockup. Six management-distance variants. Not an implementation asset.

g.text: MOCKUP D — SOUNDSTAGE WORLD-STATE LANGUAGE AT MANAGEMENT DISTANCE
Six variants of one Stage, same camera, same building. Reference only — not implementation assets. No new lifecycle state is invented: every variant below maps to existing TypeScript truth.
SHOOTING · take in progress · wk 1 of 2
Every variant is derived from state that already exists in src/core/types.ts. Nothing here adds a lifecycle state, a scene count, or a percentage.
· Shooting closes the doors. A hot set is a sealed set: red lamps lit, doors shut, interior blazing through the roofline and windows. Load-in throws them wide.
Doors alone separate the two states that today differ by 5.98% of pixels — and they read at any zoom, in any palette, without text.
· Blocked keeps its people. The company is still on the clock, so it stays on screen — grouped and idle, not deleted. An empty stage would be a lie while roles remain assigned.
· Every state is legible three ways — silhouette/light, activity, and one restrained nameplate carrying title + phase. Remove colour and all six still separate.
· One label per stage, its own holder only. A second stage renders its own current holder or nothing. Historical wrap never overrides a new occupant.
EVALUATION ORDER — THE VARIANTS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT PREDICATES
Resolve top-down and stop at the first match: Idle → Shooting → Load-In → Blocked → Wrap → Rehearsal. Load-In must be tested BEFORE Blocked, because
`scenery-load-in` is itself a blocker and would otherwise match both. A stage-anchored hold requires `bindings.stageFacilityId !== null`; a blocked picture that holds
no stage (e.g. `set-unavailable`, raised in `preProduction`) has no stage to mark and must surface on its owning building instead — never on an idle soundstage.
Not shown and deliberately absent: scene/shot counts, dailies, progress percentages, a quality meter, collapsed multi-alerts, auto-camera on state change.
Period props (camera, slate, boom, 1920s freight) are drawn here for legibility but must be withheld behind a confirmed era presentation profile — Package 05 era-safety rule.
